input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§20(h), p0146) selects Nova Scotia and Canadian law with the courts of Nova Scotia — the vendor's home jurisdiction and outside the accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales. It therefore fails both the preferred and the fallback position on a material term. The venue is non-exclusive rather than an exclusive foreign forum, so this stops short of walk-away territory, but the choice of law still requires correction. No arbitration clause exists elsewhere in the document. We propose the smallest edit to the preferred position (New York law; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County), keeping the sentence structure intact, and flag Delaware, California, or England and Wales as acceptable fallbacks.

ops.oldText: the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law and venue to our accepted New York position, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County. Nova Scotia is outside our accepted list; if helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (courts of London) as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia/Canada law and venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts.
